Good morning, founders 🕶️ 

Hope your coffee is still at the introductory price.

Every day-one price comes with a due date. Google's new flagship model costs half until _November 30_, then doubles. Adobe's $60 a month felt normal until a small team used Claude to build seven free look-alikes. And _[Character.AI](https://Character.AI)_, a unicorn in 2022, just filed for Chapter 11, with Disney paying $20 million for part of what's left. **The launch price is a loan.** Somebody repays it later: the customer, the vendor or the investors. So which of your prices, paid or charged, is running up interest right now?

In today's newsletter, we'll get into:

* How a chatbot unicorn ended at a $20M sale

* What your Gemini bill looks like on December 1

* Seven free Adobe clones, built with Claude

* Why Anthropic's investor meeting today matters if you're raising

* 🧠 Highwire, a professional-development firm, surveyed 1,034 professionals: 78% of managers used AI for feedback, only 16% of employees were told, and 34% said feedback got more generic. **[Disclose it, then add one personal question](https://www.inc.com/marcel-schwantes/78-of-managers-are-using-ai-for-employee-feedback-heres-what-they-risk-losing/91417528)**: "What's one thing I could do differently to help you succeed?"

* 🔎 Semrush, which sells AI-visibility tools, found **[fewer than half of AI's top-mentioned brands are also top-cited sources](https://thenextweb.com/news/ai-visibility-index-uk-us-semrush)**. News sites earn 19.6% of ChatGPT's top US citations.

* ⚡ AWS Lambda Web Functions **[run an unmodified Express or Next.js server](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/announcing-aws-lambda-web-functions-for-fast-consistent-web-app-performance-anywhere/)** via one command, `aws lambda-web deploy`: up to 128 concurrent requests per environment, active-CPU billing.

## Five bullets of updates

1. 🇮🇳 **India's NPCI has pushed back a 0.4% merchant fee on UPI payments over ₹2,000 (about $21), due October 15, until after Diwali, with no new date set.** Retailers and petrol pump operators had threatened to stop accepting UPI. If you sell in India, [**the fee is delayed, not dead**](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/13/india-delays-digital-payments-fee-rollout-amid-retailer-pushback/). NPCI says UPI costs about ₹200 billion a year to run, so price the fee in now.

2. 🏴‍☠️ **Prosecutors allege MonsterCloud founder Zohar Pinhasi sold "no-ransom" data recovery while secretly paying hackers more than $8M and billing clients over $19M.** In one alleged case, an $8,200 ransom became a roughly $150,000 invoice. He faces wire-fraud charges. Before you sign an incident-response vendor, [**ask exactly how it gets your data back**](https://www.inc.com/moses-jeanfrancois/cybersecurity-expert-could-beat-ransomware-prosecutors-say-paid-hackers/91418829), and get the answer in writing.

3.  🔒 **Apple unveiled its Home Collection, including a $349.95 smart lock, a $249.95 video doorbell and a $399.95 floodlight camera, built with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric and shipping in December.** That puts Apple up against Ring and Nest. Smart-home startups just gained a very rich rival. But Apple [**partnering instead of building everything itself**](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/13/apples-new-smart-home-line-up-includes-a-smart-lock-thermostat-and-video-doorbells/) shows where component makers can still get in.

4. 🎨 **A small team used Anthropic's Claude to help build ArtCraft, seven free, open-source apps that mimic Adobe Creative Cloud, from PhotoCraft to VectorCraft.** Photoshop and Illustrator run about $60 a month. Once customers resent a subscription, [**a free look-alike becomes a product**](https://www.inc.com/jason-aten/it-turns-out-the-only-thing-people-like-less-than-ai-is-paying-for-adobe-creative-cloud/91418566), and AI just made those far cheaper to build. If your churn surveys keep saying "price," your moat is thinner than you think.

5. 📊 **Anthropic plans to disclose its third-quarter financials to potential investors at a private meeting today, per two people familiar with the matter, ahead of what could be the largest IPO in history.** Anthropic declined to comment, and no listing date is confirmed. Broadcom CEO Hock Tan warned that, with rates climbing, [**access to capital could be AI's biggest constraint**](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/13/anthropic-q3-financials-ipo.html). Raising soon? Plan for tighter terms.

### **[Character.AI](https://Character.AI)****'s two exits: $2.7B to Google, $20M to Disney**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/ebd62caa-ba8d-4378-aff2-cc9c798a7cc4/gracia-dharma-qTlbO6mkQH0-unsplash.jpg?t=1791924059)
Follow image link: (https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/13/just-5-years-in-interactive-chatbot-platform-character-ai-files-for-bankruptcy/)
Caption: Photo by [Gracia Dharma](https://unsplash.com/@graciadharmaa?utm_source=unsplash&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=creditCopyText) on [Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/hands-attaching-anime-print-to-wall-qTlbO6mkQH0?utm_source=unsplash&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=creditCopyText)

Most consumer apps die because nobody uses them. _[Character.AI](https://Character.AI)_ is going under even though people used it for hours a day.

[The startup filed for ](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/13/just-5-years-in-interactive-chatbot-platform-character-ai-files-for-bankruptcy/)[**Chapter 11**](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/13/just-5-years-in-interactive-chatbot-platform-character-ai-files-for-bankruptcy/)[ on Tuesday](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/13/just-5-years-in-interactive-chatbot-platform-character-ai-files-for-bankruptcy/), listing assets and liabilities of **$50–100 million**. _Disney_ agreed to pay **$20 million** for some of its assets plus a non-exclusive, perpetual license to its tech. There's no bidder yet for the rest. That check is roughly a tenth of the **$193 million+** the company raised, per PitchBook, and it comes _four years_ after the startup hit unicorn status.

#### **Where did it break?**

**The engagement trap.** In _2022_, users averaged **more than 2 hours a day**. In most apps that's the dream. In AI, every hour of chat burns compute, so the most loyal users were also the most expensive ones.

**The brain drain.** In _August 2024_, _Google_ paid **$2.7 billion** to license the models, and founders _Noam Shazeer_ and _Daniel De Freitas_ went back to Google. [Character.AI](https://Character.AI) stopped training its own models and chased growth on a product it had stopped pushing forward.

**The lawsuits.** After a suit tied to the suicide of a 14-year-old user, plus a Texas investigation, the company settled some cases, added safety features and banned minors.

**The pivots.** Video generation, social feeds, microdramas. Then _last month_, former CEO _Karandeep Singh Anand_ and staff left for Disney, the eventual buyer.

#### **So what does a consumer-AI company actually own?**

Run the stress test on yours. Remove the model, which anyone can now rent. Remove the founders, who can leave as part of a licensing deal. What's left is users and a brand. Disney priced that at **less than 1%** of what Google paid. If "the users" is your answer, make sure each one pays more than they cost to serve.

The deadline to find a buyer for the rest is _late November or early December_. No bid, and the platform gets wound down.

### **Google's Gemini 4 Argon comes with a teaser rate**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/086a6602-576f-4ede-b496-44ef22e0752f/greg-bulla-lKjX3S4pdog-unsplash.jpg?t=1791924140)
Follow image link: (https://thenewstack.io/gemini-4-argon-live/)
Caption: Photo by [Greg Bulla](https://unsplash.com/@gregbulla?utm_source=unsplash&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=creditCopyText) on [Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-google-sign-in-front-of-some-bushes-and-trees-lKjX3S4pdog?utm_source=unsplash&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=creditCopyText)

[_Google_](https://thenewstack.io/gemini-4-argon-live/)[ just put its new flagship model on sale](https://thenewstack.io/gemini-4-argon-live/), and the sale has an end date.

_Gemini 4 Argon_ hit the paid Gemini API on Tuesday at **$2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output**, the same as _OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol_. That price runs through _November 30_. On _December 1_ it doubles to **$4/$20**, matching _Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5_. Cached input is **95% off**, and Google has only promised that discount for the intro window.

#### **Why would Google give up half the price?**

Think of it as an adjustable-rate mortgage that resets after _seven weeks_ instead of five years. Google isn't after seven weeks of revenue. It wants what you build while it's cheap. Your team wires up the `gemini-4-argon` endpoint, tunes prompts around its quirks and gets your evals passing on it. None of that work moves to another model for free.

Argon's quirks are real. Its **1 million-token** budget is shared between input and output, so an 800,000-token prompt leaves only 200,000 for the answer. _Claude Opus 5.5_ caps output separately, at **128,000**. A prompt built for one design doesn't drop cleanly into the other.

#### **What happens to your margin on December 1?**

Say your product runs **500 million** input and **100 million** output tokens a month. That's **$2,000** in _November_ and **$4,000** in _December_, before cache pricing changes anything. If you priced your plans off the promo bill, your gross margin shrinks on a date Google picked.

**The takeaway for you:** model your unit economics at $4/$20 today. Keep a second model passing your evals, and route traffic through a layer you control, so switching is a config change, not a sprint.

Watch _December 1_. Whether Google extends the promo or a rival undercuts it first will show who needed your tokens more.
